notes: The BTS Skytrain and MRT are the fastest ways to get around the city. Ask taxis to use the meter, and expect to haggle with touristy tuk-tuks. The Grab app is reliable.
Cover shoulders and knees at temples. Checks are strict at the Grand Palace, where sarongs are sold but pricey.
June to October is the rainy season, with an hour or two of downpour in the afternoon. Sightsee in the morning and save the malls for rain time. Expect 33°C and humidity.
Street food is safe: pick a busy stall, and ice is fine. Pad thai costs 60-100 THB, mango sticky rice 100 THB.
Tipping is not required, and restaurants may add a 10% service charge. Haggling is normal in markets but not in malls.
The train to Ayutthaya from Hua Lamphong takes 1.5 hours (20-60 THB). For the floating markets, take a tour or hire a car.

transit.name: Rabbit Card
transit.why_chosen: Works on the BTS Skytrain. The MRT needs a separate token or card, and both are sold at stations.

days.theme: Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun

stops.name: Grand Palace Bangkok
stops.tips: The royal palace and the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew). Entry is 500 THB, shoulders and knees must be covered. Arrive at 08:30 to beat the crowds.

stops.name: Wat Pho
stops.tips: Home to the 46 m reclining Buddha and the massage school. A 30-minute traditional massage (~300 THB) is available here.

stops.name: Tha Tien Pier
stops.tips: Cross the Chao Phraya on a 5 THB ferry. Wat Arun is right on the other side.

stops.name: Wat Arun
stops.tips: The Temple of Dawn. Climb the steep stairs of the porcelain-covered prang for river views.

stops.name: Supanniga Eating Room Tha Tien
stops.tips: Thai home cooking on the riverside. Have lunch with a view of Wat Arun: moo palo and som tam.

backups.name: Thipsamai Pad Thai
backups.tips: Bangkok's most famous pad thai. Queues build after 17:00, so lunchtime is easier.

backups.name: Museum Siam
backups.tips: An interactive Thai history museum next to Wat Pho. A good option for rainy days.

stops.name: Wat Traimit
stops.tips: Home to the 5.5-tonne golden Buddha. It marks the entrance to Chinatown.

stops.name: Yaowarat Road
stops.tips: Chinatown's main street, with gold shops, temples and quiet side streets by day.

stops.name: Talat Noi
stops.tips: An old Chinese quarter on the riverbank, full of street art, garages and cafés.

stops.name: Hua Seng Hong Yaowarat
stops.tips: A classic Chinatown Chinese restaurant. Order dim sum and goose.

stops.name: Iconsiam
stops.tips: A giant mall across the river. Street food at the Sook Siam floating market floor makes for an air-conditioned afternoon.

backups.name: Nai Ek Roll Noodle
backups.tips: Pork noodle soup on Yaowarat, a street-food classic.

backups.name: Lhong 1919
backups.tips: A restored Chinese temple and warehouse on the riverbank. Calmer than ICONSIAM.

stops.name: Jim Thompson House
stops.tips: A teak Thai house and silk collection. Visits are by guided tour, and the garden is cool.

stops.name: Siam Paragon
stops.tips: Siam's giant mall, with a food market on the lower floor. An air-conditioned break.

stops.name: Som Tam Nua Siam Square
stops.tips: Isan cooking: som tam and fried chicken. The queue moves fast at Siam Square.

stops.name: Erawan Shrine
stops.tips: A Brahma shrine in the middle of the city, with dancers and incense.

stops.name: Lumphini Park
stops.tips: Bangkok's central park, with monitor lizards, sunset and evening aerobics.

backups.name: MBK Center Food Court
backups.tips: The food court on MBK's 6th floor. Cheap and air-conditioned, an alternative to som tam.

backups.name: Benjakitti Park
backups.tips: A new wetland park, and an alternative to Lumphini.

stops.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
stops.tips: On weekends it is the world's largest market (15,000 stalls). On weekdays, head to the Or Tor Kor food market. Go early, as midday is hot.

stops.name: Or Tor Kor Market
stops.tips: A premium food market next to Chatuchak. Try the mango sticky rice and seafood.

stops.name: Ari Neighbourhood
stops.tips: Bangkok's hipster district, with cafés and boutiques. Take the BTS to Ari.

stops.name: Raan Jay Fai
stops.tips: A Michelin-starred street restaurant. Order the crab omelette (~1,000 THB). Book months ahead, or join the queue at 14:00.

backups.name: Baan Ying Ari
backups.tips: Thai home cooking in Ari. A fallback if Jay Fai doesn't work out.

backups.name: Chatuchak Park
backups.tips: A park next to the market, with shade and a lake.

stops.name: Wat Mahathat Ayutthaya
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from Bangkok by train or minivan. See the Buddha head wrapped in tree roots in this UNESCO-listed ancient capital.

stops.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
stops.tips: A royal temple with three chedis, and the symbol of Ayutthaya.

stops.name: Wat Chaiwatthanaram
stops.tips: A Khmer-style temple on the riverbank, also famous for its sunset. Go by bicycle.

stops.name: Ayutthaya Boat Noodle
stops.tips: Ayutthaya's boat noodles are served in small bowls. Eat 3 or 4.

stops.name: Ayutthaya Night Market Pier
stops.tips: A riverside market with temple views. The return train leaves at 17:00.

backups.name: Ayutthaya Roti Sai Mai
backups.tips: Cotton candy roti, Ayutthaya's signature sweet.

backups.name: Bang Pa-In Palace
backups.tips: A summer palace on the way back, with gardens and pavilions.

stops.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
stops.tips: 1.5 hours from Bangkok. The famous floating market is quieter at 08:00, and boat hire is negotiable.

stops.name: Maeklong Railway Market
stops.tips: A market set on the railway track. Check the train times (around 11:10 and 14:30).

stops.name: Amphawa Floating Market
stops.tips: A canalside market with grilled seafood served from boats. Livelier at weekends.

stops.name: Wat Bang Kung
stops.tips: A temple swallowed by a banyan tree, near Amphawa.

backups.name: Amphawa Firefly Tour
backups.tips: An evening boat tour (if you stay on) to see fireflies.

backups.name: Damnoen Saduak Boat Food Stall
backups.tips: Noodles and mango served from a boat at the floating market. Choose this if you skip Amphawa.

stops.name: Wat Saket (Golden Mount)
stops.tips: The Golden Mount: 344 steps up to 360° views of the city. Cooler in the morning.

stops.name: Bangkok Flower Market Pak Khlong Talat
stops.tips: A 24-hour flower market, with jasmine garlands and orchids.

stops.name: Baan Khanitha Sathorn
stops.tips: Classic Thai cooking in a Thai house. An air-conditioned farewell lunch.

stops.name: Lumphini MRT / Airport Rail Link
stops.tips: The airport train takes 30 minutes from Phaya Thai. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Krua Apsorn Dinso
backups.tips: Home cooking from the royal kitchen tradition. Try the crab omelette.

backups.name: Wat Suthat
backups.tips: A temple with a giant swing. Visit it instead of the Golden Mount.
